title: Other films: Calling All Stars in Britain with the Nicholas Brothers
summary: He cannot recall songs from early Pathe shorts or the story of the British film Calling All Stars, remembering only friendship with the Nicholas Brothers.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I think that as long as we're in motion pictures now, we might as well continue with the other films that you were in. We went through the days when you did the Pathé films and in those you didn't tap dance because you hadn't learned to tap dance at that point.
Not good enough.

But in particular I was wondering whether -- there was "Black Narcissus," "Foul Play," "In and Out," or "Downtown Follies," "Hightone," "Honest Crooks," were there any songs in any of these that you remember?
No songs I didn't
sing. What songs are there?
Well, I was just wondering whether you remember any songs?
I don't remember.
What about "Calling All Stars," that you did with the Nicholas Brothers. Supposedly you did that the same year that you did "Varsity Shew" in '37.
Yeah.
Was that a Hollywood film, first of all?
That was a British film, British film.
How did that come about? Was it a feature film?
Yeah, I was over there, American entertainer over there with the Nicholas Brothers, that's why they used me, I guess and I was known, too, so that makes it a little different also.
What was the story of that film?
Don't know the story. Thanks for the good question, don't know the story. It's a good question. It's all right, good question, Old Bub don't know it. Sorry.
(Chuckles)
All right. In that case if you want to skip that film --
Okay, skip it, because I can't fill it in.
What about the Nicholas Brothers, you were working with them, was there anything --
Nothing, but old-time friendship. We knew each other for quite some time, man. Good to be with them again at that time, too.
What were they doing over in England?
I think they was over there with a show or something at that time, I don't remember, don't remember.
Did Nazarro
book that one for you? I guess he must have.
